title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: W-rich refractory high-entropy alloy elemental powders blended with copper powder
recollection.intervention: powder metallurgy route involving ball milling, compacting, and spark plasma sintering (SPS) with controlled Cu infiltration
recollection.structure: bi-continuous interpenetrating network of a W-rich HEA phase and a Cu-rich phase
recollection.mechanism: the ductile Cu network provides toughness and thermal conductivity while the refractory HEA network supplies high-temperature strength and radiation resistance; strong interphase bonding arises from partial interdiffusion during SPS
recollection.results: achieved ~45 vol% Cu and ~55 vol% W-rich HEA; thermal conductivity ~280 W/m·K at 300 K; compressive yield strength ~1.1 GPa at room temperature and ~0.8 GPa at 600 °C; fracture toughness ~48 MPa·m^0.5; corrosion current density in simulated reactor coolant reduced by ~60% compared to conventional W–Cu composites

score.note: The recollection incorrectly describes powder metallurgy/SPS rather than liquid-metal dealloying of an as-cast WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu. The bicontinuous RHEA–Cu network matches only what the title broadly indicates, while omitting aligned Cu channels, phase fractions, and the ~300 nm W-rich interlayer. The functional roles assigned to Cu and the RHEA are generic; the proposed SPS interdiffusion mechanism is wrong and misses selective Ti dissolution and W-rich interfacial passivation. All reported numerical properties and phase fractions are inconsistent with the paper.
